cards.explanation: The answer is Moses. He's Israel's leader, and he's the name the writer picks. Jesus was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God's house. I bet the readers nodded right away, because nobody had to ask who he meant. Now the writer has a famous name to set Jesus beside.

The picture is a builder honored above the house. The writer says the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself, and that's how Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses. It's a simple image, and I like simple. Nobody walks into a beautiful house and gives the front door a standing ovation. They ask who built it.

The answer is True. The writer says "…every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything." That's a big sentence packed into one verse. Every house has a builder, and God is behind all of it.

The answer is as the Son over God's house. Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house, but "…Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house." Servant in the house and Son over the house are two different spots. The writer wants us to see that difference.

The answer is that we are His house. The writer says, "And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast." He doesn't stop at telling us about Christ and Moses. He tells us where we fit in, and he includes that holding firmly. Friends, that's worth catching.

The answer is False. The writer says "…we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast." He doesn't say it happens whether we hold on or not. That little word "if" does a lot of work.

The warning is against hardening your hearts. The Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts…" Notice it starts with hearing His voice. Then comes the warning about what to do with it.

The answer is forty. Forty years. The Holy Spirit says, "…where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works." Forty years of seeing what God was doing. That's a long time to have front row seats.

The answer is False. God says of that generation, "Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways." Always going astray is the opposite of finally following. He says it right after saying He was angry with that generation.
The answer is His rest. God says, "They shall never enter My rest." It was a serious oath, sworn in anger. I think that's a heavy line, and it's worth slowing down for.

The answer is unbelief. The writer warns about "…a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God." He's talking to his own brothers now, not just about people long ago. That's why he opens with "See to it, brothers…"

The answer is to urge one another on every day. The writer says, "…exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today…" The reason he gives is "…so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness." Notice the words "one another." It's a together job, friends.

The answer is True. The writer says to exhort one another daily "…so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness." He says sin can be deceitful. That's why he tells them to look out for each other.

The answer is to the end. The writer says, "We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first." Not just the start and not just the middle. Hold firmly all the way.

The answer is the people Moses led out of Egypt. The writer asks, "Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?" Moses was Israel's leader. The ones who heard and rebelled were the very people he led out.
The answer is those who sinned. The writer asks, "Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?" Forty years of anger, aimed at those who sinned. I think this part is heavy.

The answer is True. The writer asks, "And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?" He asks it as a question, and the answer is built right in. Those who disobeyed.
